Questions, answered plainly.

      
What does abliterated mean?
An abliterated model has its refusal behaviour removed at the weights level, so it answers instead of declining. Your deployment sets the policy. Unbound is abliterated by design, and Swift also comes in an abliterated variant.
How are standard, low-refusal and abliterated different?
Standard: the default behaviour of each model family. Low-refusal: fewer reflexive refusals for fiction, research and security work. Abliterated: refusal behaviour removed at the weights level. Your deployment sets the policy.
Do I need a new SDK?
No. Point the SDK you already use at Aether's base URL and change the model string. Streaming and tool calls work as before.
How is usage billed?
Per token. Input, cached input and output are priced separately for each model, and every response reports its tokens, cached tokens and cost. The rates on this page are samples for layout only.
Can I switch models in the middle of a conversation?
Yes. Unified chat carries the whole thread, files included, from one model family to the next.
What does prompt caching save?
When a long prompt prefix repeats, the repeated part is billed at the cached input rate automatically. You do not have to change your requests.
